Tensor Analysis – Practical 5 Information: • Please make sure to complete all exercises before the next lecture. • The exercises marked with [See lecture] were solved in class. • The exercises are not organised by difficulty. 5.1 [See Lecture] Write down the transformation rule for: (1) a tensor of rank four, (2) a tensor of rank six. 5.2 If Qijkℓ is a tensor of rank four, show that Qijjℓ is a tensor of rank two. 5.3 [See lecture] If Tij is a tensor, show that Tii is a scalar. 5.4 Consider the 2D polar coordinates (x1, x2) = (r, θ). In this system, the position vector r is given by r = r cos θ i1 + r sin θ i2, where i1, i2 are the usual 2-dimensional Cartesian basis vectors. (1) Find the corresponding basis vectors e1 and e2. (2) Find the covariant metric tensor gij and give your answer as a 2 × 2 matrix. Using the fact that the basis e1, e2 is orthogonal, find the contravariant metric tensor gij. (3) Give an expression for the arc length of the polar coordinate system, plus explicitly state the metric coefficients h1, h2. 5.5 In spherical coordinates (x1, x2, x3) = (r, ϕ, θ), the position vector r is given by r = r sin ϕ cos θ i1 + r sin ϕ sin θ i2 + r cos ϕ i3. Find the basis vectors and the metric coefficients. 5.6 [See Lecture] Given two vectors A and B, with components Ai and Bi, show that the second-order tensor with components Cik = AiBk − AkBi is antisymmetric. 1

2 5.7 [Question from the Main Exam 23-24] The third-rank tensor Tijk is symmetric with respect to its last two suffixes but antisymmetric with respect to its first and second suffices. Show that all entries of this tensor are zero (i.e. Tijk = 0, for all choices of i,j,k). 5.8 Let q1, q2, q3 be coordinates related to orthogonal coordinates x1, x2, x3 with orthonormal basis i1, i2, i3 by the formulae q1 = x1 + x2, q2 = x1 − x2, q3 = 2x3. (1) Find the corresponding basis vectors and show that they form an orthogonal basis. [Hint: Using r = x1i1 + x2i2 + x3i3, you need to find expressions for x1, x2, x3 in terms of q1, q2, q3 and substitute these into your expansion for r.] (2) Find the metric tensor gik and give your answer as a matrix. Using the fact that the basis e1, e2, e3 is orthogonal, find the contravariant metric tensor gik. (3) Give an expression for the arc length of the coordinate system with respect to the basis e1, e2, e3. (4) Find the covariant and contravariant components of the vectors A = 2i1, B = i1 + i2, C = 2i1 − 3i3, with respect to the basis e1, e2, e3, but without computing the dual basis e1, e2, e3. 5.9 Given two generalised coordinate systems, with bases e1, e2, e3 and e′ 1, e′ 2, e′ 3, respec- tively, suppose that the position vector x has coordinates (x1, x2, x3) with respect to e1, e2, e3 and suppose that x has coordinates (x′1, x′2, x′3) with respect to e′ 1, e′ 2, e′ 3. Let L j i′ be the coefficients of the direct transformation and L j′ i the coefficients of the inverse transformation. Given the following alternative definitions: L j i′ = ∂xj ∂x′i , L i′ j = ∂x′i ∂xj , show that g.j i = L k′ i L j k′.
